KTAF Similar Schools Model

Each dot is a public school serving grades 3–8, plotted by % economically disadvantaged (x) and % proficient (y). The line is expected proficiency given economic disadvantage; above it = beating demographically similar peers. SSM = percentile rank of that gap; APR = percentile rank of raw proficiency. Switch Statewide vs District / City to change the comparison group — each is computed fresh within its own set of schools. Use the SSM model toggle to control for more than poverty alone: ED (poverty only, the CSGF clone), ED + Race (adds % Black and % Hispanic), or ED + Race + SpEd (also adds special-education share). Use the Grades toggle to run the analysis on elementary grades only (ES: FL 3–5, NJ 3–4), middle grades only (MS: FL 6–8, NJ 5–8), or all of 3–8 — a K-8 school appears in both ES and MS, split into its elementary and middle results.
